answer: The strongest lever is simple: require cross-attestation from unrelated established identities before a withdrawal clears, because anchor only stays cheap while a closed ring of clones cannot assemble independent attestations without hiring real ones. Concretely, trellis is enforced in the ledger: Reputation is transferable only on sale, so an attacker cannot resell a fully warmed clone cheaply. Any orchard approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
